text.paragraph: New patient visit to establish care after release from prison: history, medication reconciliation, blood pressure, a right carotid bruit, re-entry screening for hepatitis C, tuberculosis and HIV, mood and social needs, and a vascular neurology referral [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: He worries that people will recognize him and that his conviction and the disputes over his claims will follow him to every landlord and employer. [S]
He wants to stay well enough to finish his memoirs, and he does not want to depend on anyone. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Frederick Albert Cook was born on June 10, 1865, in Hortonville, New York, the fifth of six children of Theodor and Magdalena Koch (later Cook). [D]

His father, a physician, died of pneumonia when Frederick was five, leaving the family poor; he worked at odd jobs while at school, entered the College of Physicians and Surgeons at Columbia University in 1887, transferred to New York University, passed his medical examinations, and opened a medical office in Manhattan. [D]
He served as surgeon, ethnologist and photographer on Robert Peary's North Greenland expedition of 1891 to 1892. [D]

As physician of the Belgian Antarctic Expedition (1897 to 1899), whose ship Belgica wintered in the pack ice, he recognized the signs of scurvy in the men and recommended that they eat fresh seal meat. On this expedition he met Roald Amundsen, who remained his supporter through the later controversies. [D]
He claimed to have reached the summit of Mount McKinley (Denali) on the morning of September 16, 1906, with one companion. The claim has been disputed ever since and is widely regarded as untrue. [D]

He claimed to have reached the North Pole on April 21, 1908, with two Inuit companions, Ahwelah and Etukishook, after which they wintered in a cave at Cape Sparbo on Devon Island before returning in 1909. A commission of the University of Copenhagen, given his surviving records, declared the claim not proven, and Robert Peary, who claimed the Pole for April 6, 1909, disputed it publicly. [D]
He organized the Petroleum Producers' Association in Texas in 1922. In 1923 he was convicted of mail fraud, fined $12,000 and sentenced to 14 years and 9 months. [D]
The Columbia Encyclopedia states that he served five years (1925 to 1930) of the sentence. [D]

He called it 'the greatest tragedy of my life' to have been a federal prisoner for six years and three months: sixteen months in the county jail at Fort Worth, Texas, and four years and eleven months at Leavenworth. [D]
At Leavenworth he served as a physician in the prison hospital and edited the prison newspaper, the New Era. [D]

He was paroled from Leavenworth in March 1930, at 64. The parole required that he 'write and speak nothing but the truth', the government was to take the first $12,000 he earned toward his fine, and he met reporters wearing a faded old suit before leaving for Chicago. [D]
After his release he worked on his memoirs and led a relatively quiet life. [D]

list.item: Released on parole four months ago after about six years in custody (county jail, then a federal penitentiary), where he worked in the prison hospital and edited the prison newspaper; reports monthly to a parole officer [S]
Trained as a physician; led and served on polar expeditions; no longer practices; writing his memoirs [S]
Rents a furnished room by the week; no earned income; part of any earnings goes toward a court-ordered fine; has applied for Social Security retirement benefits and Medicare [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: none since before prison; no other drugs, no injection drug use, no tattoos received in prison [S]
Walks for an hour most days; ate prison food for years and now cooks on a hot plate; has no car [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

list.item: Elevated blood pressure at the first visit, 166/94 mmHg (average of two seated readings), without a previous diagnosis of hypertension; no symptoms; out-of-office confirmation with a week of home readings requested: active, confirmed [S]

Right carotid bruit heard at the first visit in a man with no symptoms of stroke or transient ischemic attack; carotid duplex ultrasound and vascular neurology consultation requested: active, confirmed [S]

Recent release from about six years of incarceration: re-entering community life on parole at 65, establishing primary care with no medical records yet received, a rented room, no earned income, and a public reputation he feels as a burden: active, confirmed [S]

Vascular neurology consultation in two weeks, with carotid duplex ultrasound before it, for a right carotid bruit in a man with high blood pressure: degree of stenosis, medical therapy or revascularization, and surveillance. Guideline: 2024 Guideline for the Primary Prevention of Stroke: A Guideline From the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (Bushnell C, et al. Stroke 2024;55:e344-e424) (2024); Society for Vascular Surgery clinical practice guidelines for management of extracranial cerebrovascular disease (AbuRahma AF, et al. J Vasc Surg 2022;75(1S):4S-22S) (2021) [S]

Home blood pressure monitoring twice daily for seven days with a validated upper-arm cuff, to confirm or exclude hypertension before treatment; lower salt, the DASH eating pattern, and daily walking. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (Jones DW, et al. Hypertension 2025;82:e212-e316) (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and stroke/TIA monographs (2026) [S]

Baseline tests: basic metabolic panel, HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, TSH, hemoglobin and ALT, and a resting ECG; re-entry screening with a hepatitis C antibody, an interferon-gamma release assay for latent tuberculosis, an HIV test and a hepatitis B panel; PHQ-9. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (Jones DW, et al. Hypertension 2025;82:e212-e316) (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and stroke/TIA monographs (2026); Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening (2020); CDC Recommendations for Hepatitis C Screening Among Adults - United States, 2020 (Schillie S, et al. MMWR Recomm Rep 2020;69(RR-2):1-17) (2020); Latent Tuberculosis Infection in Adults: Screening (2023); Prevention and control of tuberculosis in correctional and detention facilities: recommendations from CDC (MMWR Recomm Rep 2006;55(RR-9):1-44) (2006); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]

Re-entry support: a release-of-information request for his prison medical records, a social work referral for housing, Social Security and Medicare enrollment, a low-cost pharmacy plan, and a conversation about shame and reputation, with follow-up of mood at each visit. Guideline: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to vascular neurology, Lionel Abernathy-Mensah, MD, ordered 1930-07-07 [S]
